# Incident Report — MTA 2026-02-28: NetSupport RAT Infection

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.2.28.88** |
| MAC address | **00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR** |
| Windows domain/workgroup | EASYAS123 (AD domain `easyas123.tech`, DC at 10.2.28.2 / EASYAS123-DC) |
| Logged-in user account | **brolf** (observed as Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ traffic sourced from 10.2.28.88) |

Confirmed via DHCP Request (frames 2/103, option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR`, requested IP `10.2.28.88`) and corroborating NBNS name registrations (`DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR<00>/<20>`, workgroup `EASYAS123<00>/<1e>`) from the same source IP/MAC.

## 2. Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (malicious abuse of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client as a commodity RAT/loader payload).

**Attribution basis: signature-confirmed.**
- The `User-Agent` header on every C2 request is literally `NetSupport Manager/1.3`.
- The application-layer protocol is the documented NetSupport client-server handshake: POST body decodes to `CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1\n`, and the server response begins `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<hex-encoded blob>`. This exact `CMD=`/`ENCD` framing is the NetSupport proprietary protocol, not generic malware traffic guessed from context — both the UA string and the protocol grammar independently confirm the family.
- Traffic is sent to TCP/443 but is plaintext HTTP (no TLS ClientHello on that stream), a known NetSupport RAT evasion trait (using the "HTTPS port" without actually using TLS).

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `45.131.214.85:443` (TCP, plaintext HTTP masquerading as port 443/TLS) — active beaconing from infection (frame 2638, t=45.0s) through the end of the capture, POST `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm`, polling roughly every 60 seconds after the initial burst.

**Malicious domain:**
- `vadusa.xyz` — resolved by victim DNS query (frame 1559/1747, t=44.77s) to `45.131.214.85` (frame 2566), immediately preceding first C2 contact.

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` — C2 check-in/exfil endpoint, identical path used on every POST/response pair observed.

**Infection-chain context (not independently malicious but evidentiary):**
- Victim resolved and browsed `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (A record `23.64.147.24`, legitimate Akamai-hosted government site) at t=44.44s, only ~0.33s before the `vadusa.xyz` lookup at t=44.77s — consistent with a redirect/lure chain (e.g., a spoofed FMCSA compliance page or ClickFix-style fake-CAPTCHA prompt) driving the victim to attacker infrastructure. First C2 beacon to 45.131.214.85 fires at t=45.05s, roughly 0.6s after the `vadusa.xyz` DNS answer.

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- None recoverable. The NetSupport C2 channel uses its proprietary `CMD=ENCD` encoded/obfuscated payload format over plaintext HTTP, not a standard file transfer (no `Content-Disposition`, no recognizable executable MIME type, no exported binary object in the capture). No `.exe`/`.msi`/`.dll`/`.zip` download was observed anywhere in the capture's HTTP objects (all other exported HTTP objects belong to legitimate Microsoft/Adobe/MSN telemetry and update traffic). Consequently, **no SHA256 can be computed from this evidence** — the initial-access payload (whatever dropped/launched the NetSupport client) is not present in this PCAP.

## Summary

Host DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), logged in as user `brolf` on the EASYAS123 domain, was redirected from a browsing session touching `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` to the attacker domain `vadusa.xyz`, which resolved to `45.131.214.85`. Within under a second, the host began beaconing to `45.131.214.85:443` using the NetSupport Manager client protocol (`User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, `POST /fakeurl.htm`, `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` framing), continuing periodic check-ins for the remainder of the capture — signature-confirmed NetSupport RAT C2 activity. The delivery mechanism for the NetSupport client itself is not captured in this PCAP.
